entry.title: Make space for everyone’s needs
entry.summary: Bring the adults’ needs into the family conversation too. Look together at the care, rest, company, and practical work that need room in the coming days.
entry.cue: When family plans seem to leave someone’s needs out.
detail: If you share care, check how the other person is doing and what support would help. The Baby authors suggest a regular chance to discuss arrangements, what is working, and what needs adjusting.

Davies describes planning around different needs, such as errands, rest, friendship, and a child’s wish to play. Her example looks for a workable combination rather than making the child’s enjoyment a reward for being good.

The books recognize many forms of family and support. A partner, relatives, or friends may have a part, according to who is in your life. Start with what is possible; the conversation need not produce a perfect solution.

principle.text: The child’s needs belong alongside the needs of the family.
